name: Schneider Electric Infrastructure Ltd
title: Schneider Electric Infrastructure Ltd - 534139 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 orders hit a record INR 915 crore but EBIT fell to INR 32 crore on commodity-driven gross margin squeeze from legacy fixed-price orders; management gave no numeric guidance and pricing actions are yet to fructify.

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 order intake hit a record INR 915 crore (+0.5% YoY, double-digit QoQ) but EBIT fell to INR 32 crore on gross margin pressure and negative operating leverage.
summary.overview: Management reported a record quarterly order booking of INR 915 crore, with sales growing about 5% YoY in a seasonally soft Q1 and an order backlog of about INR 2,100 crore entering Q2, up around 33%. EBIT was INR 32 crore, lower than last year, as commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, transformer wire) and legacy fixed-price contracts compressed gross margin, while employee and other costs rose faster than sales. Management attributed the margin dip largely to Q1 operating leverage and FX-driven import costs, and said pricing actions are underway but will take time to flow through. No numerical guidance was given; management said the balance three quarters should be good.

financial_highlights.change: +0.5% YoY; double-digit QoQ growth; highest-ever quarterly order booking
Dipped YoY due to commodity inflation and legacy fixed-price orders
Flat QoQ; YoY increase due to non-cash fair-value accounting gain in last year's Q1
Management cited ~1.9% figure tied to GM pressure and negative operating leverage

segments.name: Power & Grid
segments.commentary: Management said legacy margin pressure is concentrated in Power & Grid, where orders booked before December 2025 carry firm prices; secondary distribution equipment and transformers are mainly Power & Grid products.

segments.name: Emerging segments (data centres, semiconductors)
segments.commentary: Management said more than one-fifth of the order bank now comes from emerging segments; a semiconductor transformer order was described as the largest front-end fab order received, and a data-centre MV panel order was also won.

segments.name: Metals & Mining
segments.commentary: Management said traction is being seen with a healthy pipeline in the MMM segment, without quantification.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue is 10-12% of revenue; the new Kolkata plant is expected to cater to exports, which are only starting to ramp.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue or margin guidance given; management declined to give forward-looking figures for Q2 or FY27.
Management said Q2 is expected to do better than Q1 historically, and that the forward-looking three quarters are good for the company.
Pricing actions have been initiated across standard price-list products but will take time to fructify.
Capacity expansions across the Baroda medium-voltage plant, Baroda transformer plant and Kolkata plant are on track, with some completing in calendar 2027 and some in 2028, followed by ramp-up.
Management expects the commodity tailwinds to moderate and margin headwinds to iron out over time.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR 500 crore of capex deployed over the last three years across the company's three plants, aimed at capacity additions and cutting imports from other Schneider factories.
Kolkata plant began capitalisation and operations early in FY27; depreciation is rising and is expected to be accelerated by plant growth.
Multiple capex programmes (Baroda MV factory, Baroda transformer factory, Kolkata plant) have staggered completion timelines and ramp-up plans, all tracking to plan per management.
Company said it is aligned with government capex, including RDSS of about INR 3,00,000 crore, to address secondary distribution and transformer demand.
demand_pricing: Order intake of INR 915 crore was a record quarterly figure; management said Q1 order timing included spillover of 15-20% at times, varying quarter to quarter.
Commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, labour) and INR depreciation of about 8% YTD are the key headwinds cited.
Legacy contracts booked before December 2025 are largely fixed-price; the company cannot always revise prices, hitting gross margin, mostly in Power & Grid.

Price variation clauses cover about 20-25% of the backlog, mainly large execution cycle projects over 6 months to 1 year; mandatory PVC is now being put into new contracts, but not in government tenders.
Imports are 10-15% of COGS, roughly matched by export revenue, providing a natural FX hedge.
Management said pipeline for Power & Grid is healthy, including private utility inquiries, and expects both volume growth and price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin miss driven by lack of operating leverage, and what is the outlook for other expenses growth of ~20% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q1 squeeze is a normal Q1 effect of annual salary increments and cost inflation from 1 April, combined with moderate sales growth of ~5%. Other expenses rose on FX and an 8-10% regular cost inflation; management expects it to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will you quantify FY27 revenue expectations given the backlog growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers; said Q2 historically does better than Q1 and that the remaining three quarters look good, and that pricing actions are underway.

qa_highlights.question: Are legacy orders (pre-December) hurting margins, and how much of the backlog has price variation protection?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-December orders are largely firm-price; about 20-25% of backlog has price variation clauses; new contracts now carry mandatory PVC except in government tenders where bids are price-fixed with validity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 order growth is fresh versus spillover from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said spillover from March into April is normal, sometimes 15-20%, sometimes less; it could not quantify it precisely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export share and medium-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are 10-12% of revenue; management declined to give a percentage target but said absolute export value will rise with the Kolkata plant.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable distribution (DISCOM) capex TAM and how selective are you?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is selective, bidding only on strategic accounts with visible sites and lower execution ambiguity; it avoids underground cabling and substation civil work and focuses on equipment and grid modernisation within RDSS.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on pricing actions taking hold and commodity costs stabilising; no quantified price increase was disclosed.
Legacy fixed-price contracts (pre-December 2025) and government tenders without price variation clauses keep margin exposed to commodity and FX moves.
Execution delays on customer projects could again hit gross margin, per management.
Rising INR depreciation (about 8% YTD) affects imported components and FX-linked other expenses.
Next quarter to monitor: EBIT recovery vs Rs 32 crore base, transactional vs systems revenue mix (management to provide from next quarter), and new capacity commissioning in Baroda and Kolkata.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the pipeline but cautious and somewhat evasive on margins and FY27 numbers; management repeatedly declined to quantify price increases, Q2 outlook or TAM and attributed the Q1 margin miss mainly to timing and external factors.
